Julia (Tide Inc): Hey @support — after the reserved variant freeze last night our embeddings started failing. Our index started throwing shape errors: expected 1536 but got 2048. Request id req_abc123. This started ~2026-03-16T21:15Z. Can you help?
Ana (support): Thanks, Julia — opening an escalation. Can you paste a minimal request/response and the client error?
Julia (Tide Inc): Snippet below. We get a normal 200 but vector length is 2048. Client indexer fails on ingest.
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model":"open-embed-alpha-locked-v2",
  "input":"..."
}
---
200 OK
{
  "data":[{ "embedding_length": 2048, "embedding_sample":"<truncated>" }]
}

Indexer error: IndexerError: expected vector length 1536 got 2048
```
Ana (support): Ack — assigning to eng + ops. @Matt @Sara @Deepak can you check the alias/variant mapping and recent deploys?
deploy-bot: deploy log: reserved-capacity-failover at 2026-03-16T21:12Z; automation-run id=auto-ff22; alias open-embed-alpha-locked now points -> open-embed-alpha-v2-quant (previously v1).
Matt (eng): Looking at model registry now. open-embed-alpha-v2 metadata shows embedding_size=2048. The alias open-embed-alpha-locked is pointing to v2. That would explain the jump. Not sure why alias changed if it was supposed to be locked.
Deepak (ops): Checked failover automation: during a reserved pool failover the automation tried to remap aliases for capacity balancing. It looks like the script didn't respect the locked flag on a subset of aliases (race condition).
Sara (ml): From quality side v2 is different (2048). For backward compatibility options: 1) rollback alias to v1 (1536) — client impact minimal but customers expecting v2 would change; 2) offer on-the-fly projection/truncation (server-side) to 1536 — lossy and may break semantics; 3) ask customers to reindex to 2048 (not feasible for large indexes).
Julia (Tide Inc): Reindexing 2.5B docs is impossible short-term. We need rollback to 1536 ASAP. Short maintenance window ok.
Ana (support): Understood. @deploy-bot, initiate alias rollback to open-embed-alpha-v1 for open-embed-alpha-locked (per Tide request). Please include a 10-minute maintenance notice.
deploy-bot: starting alias-rollback workflow id=rb-9001. Notifying affected customers. Maintenance window: immediate (~10m).
Matt (eng): Performing alias revert now. Will monitor in-flight requests and KV caches.
Deepak (ops): Ops note: we should throttle routing during alias changes to avoid mixing vector dims in pipelines. Enabling temporary request draining.
Matt (eng): Rollback completed at 2026-03-16T21:36Z. Registry now shows alias open-embed-alpha-locked -> open-embed-alpha-v1 (embedding_size=1536).
Ana (support): @Julia can you re-run the failing ingest and confirm?
Julia (Tide Inc): Re-ran — embeddings now 1536, indexer accepts docs. Thanks, this fixed it 👍
Ana (support): Great. Filing internal incident and RCA. INF-7843 created and assigned to ops automation team.
Deepak (ops): I'll own the RCA. Preliminary root cause: automation did not check alias.locked flag during failover remapping; race condition with concurrent alias sync job. Patch submitted (PR #1442) to enforce locking and add unit tests. ETA 48h to rollout safe fix and integration test.
Sara (ml): Adding a low-effort safety: model-metadata webhook to alert when embedding_size changes for any alias. Starting PR.
Julia (Tide Inc): Appreciate the quick rollback. Please confirm when automation patch is live so we can feel safe to use reserved variants again.
Ana (support): We'll follow up in INF-7843 with timeline and postmortem. If you want an SLA credit or temporary dedicated window, I can escalate.
Julia (Tide Inc): Not necessary right now. Would like a heads-up when fix is in prod.
Matt (eng): Noted. Also adding a guard in the alias mutation API to reject swaps that change embedding_size unless explicitly overridden — another safety net.
Ana (support): Closing thread for now; reopening if any anomalies. Thanks everyone.
